change: Linux framebuffer services DMA completions between bounded native drawing rows and cache chunks while preserving caller IRQ state; boot-persistent timing/poll counters and updated diagnostic.
components: Kernel and NOMMU userspace rebuilt; loader application descriptor rebuilt with corrected metadata dependency. HOME refresh code and factory template unchanged from revision 37.

host_tests.command: CROSS_COMPILE=<pinned P4 toolchain prefix> python3 -B -m unittest discover -s tests -v

coverage: IRQ-masked 160 ms bulk draw negative control versus row-bounded completion polling; caller IRQ state preserved.
Pixel checks for COPY/XOR fills, vertical/horizontal overlapping copies, mono byte padding and color stride.
DMA errors take precedence over completion; inactive and faulted scanout cannot restart through polling.
Existing descriptor invalidation/publication, bounded cache chunks, fixed geometry, palette and backlight regressions.
Diagnostic runs with pinned NOMMU hush; missing timing/polling counters and DMA/stall/underrun failures are rejected.
display_checks.model_timing: 200 us per native row; old bulk control services after 160000 us; bounded callbacks maximum serviced-completion interval 16800 us. Model timings are not physical measurements.

incremental_metadata_dependency: launcher/metadata.json is a CMake configure input; packaging checks ESP app descriptor version against metadata and rejects cached older versions.
limitations: IRQ-local serialization relies on the single-core production build; framebuffer Kconfig excludes SMP and packaging checks it.
Polling and maximum service interval are diagnostic observations, not a guarantee that every DSI FIFO deadline was met.
Native models do not emulate panel scanout, PSRAM contention or all boot interrupt-masked sections.
remaining: User device test for startup blue flashes, m5-display-test output, standalone boot and clean shutdown/relaunch.
Remaining first-run home creation/reset/durability/interruption device qualification.
